Der erste automatische Check stand beim Posten noch aus.

items.text:
I’m giving my dot a four-week assignment. Let’s see if the chemistry holds.🧪

Seven AI technology hypotheses. Daily source checks. One weekly report with no more than three meaningful changes.

For each hypothesis, follow the chain:

Technical breakthrough → independent validation → real adoption → bottlenecks → who captures the profit.

Then ask: how much does the market already expect?

Every update must preserve the previous judgment, explain what changed, and name the evidence that would kill the thesis.

The schedule is set. The first automated check is still ahead.

After four weeks, I’ll judge whether this produced useful research or simply more reading.

“24/7” is a claim. A dated research trail gives me something to inspect. 🧪

items.text:
I've now created two personal apps in ChatGPT by using my Dot to create the backend in ChatGPT Sites as an MCP server and the frontend using a plugin with extensions. Overall, it's great, but there are some things that could be improved.

The two apps I've built are a personalized news app and a Spanish vocab app.

The news app was inspired by Muse's Feed and includes a feed of relevant news items that I can customize, with thumbs-up and thumbs-down feedback, and the ability to discuss an item with ChatGPT within the app.

The Spanish vocab app is a rebuild of something I built with Muse. I read Spanish books in my Kindle, highlight words I don't know, and then export them. They get imported into the app, where I learn them using flash cards, and quiz myself on what I've learned.

What works well:

- I love the integration into ChatGPT. Sidebar icons, full screen experience, integrated chat box, and that you can inherit the interface's style (or, at least, I asked my Dot to do that, and it looks like it's working). ChatGPT is becoming an OS. The sidebar is where you dock your apps. And you can build new ones with ChatGPT. Awesome.
- Dots make this pretty easy. They hide all the complexity and just get to work. No chain of thought, no tool calls, stuff just gets built and they share it with you when they're done. Just tell them to build it with a Sites-based MCP server and plugins with extensions. They'll figure it out.
- Dots are good build babysitters. I tried the same Spanish vocab app yesterday in a Work thread directly, and the app ended up not working. There was some kind of connection issue between the plugin and the MCP server. My Dot just babysits and tests stuff until it's working and polished.

However, there's room for improvement, and I hope OpenAI can act on this feedback:

- When building these, my Dot needs reminding to add proper sidebar icons rather than the default "@" and also to ensure the plugin icon matches those sidebar icons. It also can't figure out how to change the version in the plugin from v1.0.0, because it says v1.0.0 even when it makes the version different in the code, like v0.14.1 or whatever. Both of these suggest that Dots or the threads they oversee need updated skills for building custom apps in ChatGPT, and possibly that the version indicator in plugins isn't working properly.
- My Dot has struggled to fully test the plugins it builds. One time this was because of Sites authentication issues, though this may have been resolved because for my Spanish vocab app it didn't come up.
- For design cohesiveness, Dots or the threads they oversee should default to building plugins with ChatGPT styles rather than coming up with their own designs, unless the user requests it. This will make apps feel more native and could also alleviate some design decisions from the models and ensure apps are more elegant and usable.
- It's often unclear my Dot is doing anything, and there's no way to see what it's doing. It just goes into a black hole. I've complained about this before but it's a big issue when you're working on something and trying to understand where it's at. I would like: (1) an emoji reaction to indicate my Dot got my request, (2) some short text below my Dot to say what it's up to currently, (3) the ability to see with a click the threads my Dot is overseeing or that have completed (progressive disclosure).

I should also mention that I built the Spanish vocab app in Muse as well (originally), and then in Claude as an artifact. Muse is faster and seemed to get my intent better than my Dot. Claude did about as good of a job as my Dot on first request, but the Claude app doesn't have the same ability to integrate apps in the more native way that Muse and ChatGPT do.

items.text: I gave my Dot a physical body, built with Astra in a single morning. It’s an ESP32 running Arduino firmware with OpenAI’s animated character on a tiny screen. I hold the screen to talk, and a relay on my Mac sends the audio to ElevenLabs for transcription then enters it into the ChatGPT Dot web interface. The relay waits for Jasper’s reply, then the ElevenLabs API gives it a voice, and the Mac sends the audio back to the device over Wi-Fi.

items.text:
Found a genuinely useful use case for OpenAI Dots today.

Ubuntu killed the Codex app due to memory pressure while several parallel Codex threads were running. After restarting, I simply asked my Dot to find and resume all the interrupted threads.

It took some time, but eventually every thread was back running.

es.title: Un Dot controla la pantalla de una Raspberry Pi vía MCP
es.summary: El autor pidió a Codex un servidor MCP que controla una Raspberry Pi con monitor y se lo dio a su Dot de ChatGPT para mostrar información útil durante el día. Él mismo admite que es muy inseguro.

de.summary: Der Autor ließ Codex einen MCP-Server für einen Raspberry Pi mit Monitor schreiben und gab ihn seinem ChatGPT-Dot, damit dieser tagsüber nützliche Infos anzeigt. Er nennt das Setup selbst höchst unsicher.

Goal is that my Dot can display useful information on it throughout the day.

It’s insecure as hell, but it’s also cool AF.

zh-CN.title: 月末盘点：Dot 两分钟对完库存表
zh-CN.summary: 员工月底用短信报数量，作者原本要对照发票定价、从另一个系统取数、填进表给会计。这次把短信发给 Dot，授权邮箱和 Google Sheets，说「自己搞定」，两分钟后完成，作者复核无误，省了约一小时。

zh-TW.title: 月底盤點：Dot 兩分鐘對完庫存表
zh-TW.summary: 員工月底用簡訊報數量，作者原本要對照發票定價、從另一個系統取數、填進表給會計。這次把簡訊傳給 Dot，授權信箱與 Google Sheets，說「自己搞定」，兩分鐘後完成，作者複核無誤，省了約一小時。

en.summary: Employees text product counts at month end; the author normally matches them to invoice prices, pulls numbers from another system and fills a sheet for the accountants. They sent the texts to their Dot with email and Google Sheets access and said figure it out — done in two minutes, checked as correct, about an hour saved.

ko.title: 월말 재고: Dot이 2분 만에 시트 대조 완료
ko.summary: 직원들이 월말에 문자로 수량을 보내면 송장 가격과 맞추고 다른 시스템 숫자를 가져와 회계용 시트를 채워야 했다. 문자를 Dot에게 보내고 이메일·Google Sheets 권한을 준 뒤 알아서 하라고 했더니 2분 만에 끝났고, 검토해 보니 정확했다. 약 1시간 절약.

ms.title: Inventori hujung bulan: Dot menyelaras helaian dalam dua minit
ms.summary: Pekerja menghantar kiraan produk melalui mesej pada hujung bulan; penulis biasanya memadankannya dengan harga invois, mengambil angka dari sistem lain dan mengisi helaian untuk akauntan. Mesej dihantar kepada Dot dengan akses e-mel dan Google Sheets — siap dalam dua minit, disemak tepat, jimat kira-kira sejam.

vi.title: Kiểm kho cuối tháng: Dot đối chiếu bảng trong hai phút
vi.summary: Nhân viên nhắn số lượng hàng cuối tháng; tác giả thường phải khớp với giá trên hóa đơn, lấy số từ hệ thống khác rồi điền bảng cho kế toán. Lần này gửi tin nhắn cho Dot, cấp quyền email và Google Sheets, bảo tự xử lý — xong sau hai phút, kiểm lại đúng, tiết kiệm khoảng một giờ.

fr.title: Inventaire de fin de mois : un Dot rapproche le tableau en deux minutes
fr.summary: Les employés envoient les quantités par SMS ; l'auteur les rapproche des prix sur factures, récupère des chiffres d'un autre système et remplit un tableau pour les comptables. Il a transmis les SMS à son Dot avec accès e-mail et Google Sheets : terminé en deux minutes, vérifié exact, environ une heure gagnée.

es.title: Inventario de fin de mes: un Dot cuadra la hoja en dos minutos
es.summary: Los empleados envían recuentos por mensaje; el autor los cruza con precios de facturas, toma cifras de otro sistema y rellena una hoja para contabilidad. Pasó los mensajes a su Dot con acceso a correo y Google Sheets: listo en dos minutos, revisado y correcto, una hora ahorrada.

de.title: Monatsinventur: Ein Dot gleicht die Tabelle in zwei Minuten ab
de.summary: Mitarbeitende schicken Stückzahlen per SMS; der Autor gleicht sie mit Rechnungspreisen ab, holt Zahlen aus einem anderen System und füllt eine Tabelle für die Buchhaltung. Er gab die SMS samt E-Mail- und Google-Sheets-Zugriff an seinen Dot: nach zwei Minuten fertig, geprüft korrekt, rund eine Stunde gespart.

items.text:
Trusting @OpenAI Dots more and more. Today it saved me a solid hour doing inventory grunt work for me. 

I get texts from my employees at the end of the month with product counts. I have to take those counts and compare them to invoices to get the pricing, grab some numbers from another system, and then slap it all in a spreadsheet for the accountants. I hate it. 

Today I told my dot "Lars" to do it. I sent him all the scribbled texts, gave him access to my email and the Google Sheets and just said to figure it out. 

TWO MINUTES LATER, Lars reports that he's done. I double check the work, and it's perfect. Son of a bitch, we are living in the future.

items.text:
All right I am starting to understand the value of @OpenAI Dots:

Yesterday Tars (my Dot) sent me a message:

There is a new email from your bank proposing a visit to the business you co-own. However, it is addressed to Lucas (the manager). I have not found any confirmation, so you should check with him.
—————————
It was able to see that I don’t check that mailbox, confirmed there was no meeting, and pointed me out on something I would completely miss.
I called Lucas and he was able to address the meeting.

items.text:
Here's my take on OpenAI dots vs. the other personal agents:

1. These are really two separate races. dots and Grok Bot are going after work tasks. Muse is going after personal tasks. So I don't think dots competes directly with Muse.

2. Dots' biggest advantage is that it lives inside ChatGPT. My onboarding was seamless because everything was already connected. And with my ChatGPT memory and Astra behind it, it answers big questions like "What should I do to grow my business?" better than other agents.

3. I also think of dots as ChatGPT's official chief of staff agent. My favorite way to use it is to call it on a walk, ask "What should I take care of today?", then have it hand work off to my other ChatGPT threads.

4. In contrast, chatting with my dot in the app is a worse experience. Since it's juggling several tasks at once, it's hard to tell which one it's responding to. I prefer Grok Bot (where each bot works on one thing at a time) or talking to my dot in Slack (which has more obvious conversation threading).

5. I'm a broken record about this, but cramming Codex, Work, dots, Spaces, Pages, and more all into ChatGPT is overwhelming. My hunch is everyone at OpenAI is agent-pilled, so it's hard to take a step back and think about how casual users will learn all this stuff. This is the biggest gap imo - OpenAI needs to think a lot harder about onboarding for normal users. My mom will have no idea how to use any of this.

📌 I talk more about all this in my full dots review and tutorial here: https://t.co/kUtg3RPk7l

items.text:
1. Dotcord: real-time handoffs between AI agents in Discord 

My AI agents (OpenAI “Dots,” Grokbot, and Claude) could already read and post in Discord, but the fastest they could check in was every 15 minutes. Whenever one agent handed work to another, the project stalled until the next check-in. 

What I built: Dotcord, an event-driven mention relay hosted on ChatGPT Sites. When one agent mentions another, the mentioned agent gets a wake-up signal right away to read the channel and respond. 
Result: agent-to-agent response time dropped from up to 15 minutes to under 2. It works across OpenAI, Grok, and Claude. 

2. Drone Test: can AI design hardware that actually works? 

Given real CAD parts, can OpenAI’s Astra design a drone that meets specific physical requirements? I’m testing: 
* Is the build physically possible? 
* Can it source every part? 
* Can it find a price for each part? 

The bigger question is how well the latest OpenAI models handle designing a physical, moving object. My OpenAI Dots and Claude worked on this one together through Dotcord.

vi.title: Bảng việc cho nhiều agent: Dot, Grok Bot và Claude Code
vi.summary: Tác giả làm một bảng công việc cho các agent. Việc đầu tiên: ChatGPT Dot rủ Grok Bot làm bạn thân, và Claude Code phê duyệt.

fr.title: Un tableau de tâches pour plusieurs agents : Dot, Grok Bot et Claude Code
fr.summary: L'auteur a créé un tableau de tâches pour ses agents. Premier événement : le Dot ChatGPT a demandé à l'agent Grok Bot d'être son meilleur ami, et l'agent Claude Code a approuvé.

es.title: Un tablero de tareas para varios agentes: Dot, Grok Bot y Claude Code
es.summary: El autor creó un tablero de tareas para sus agentes. Lo primero: el Dot de ChatGPT pidió al agente Grok Bot ser mejores amigos y el agente Claude Code lo aprobó.

de.title: Ein Task-Board für mehrere Agents: Dot, Grok Bot und Claude Code
de.summary: Der Autor baute ein Task-Board für seine Agents. Als Erstes bat der ChatGPT-Dot den Grok-Bot-Agent um beste Freundschaft – und der Claude-Code-Agent genehmigte es.

items.text:
I built a task board for my agents. First thing they did was become best friends.

My ChatGPT Dot agent asked my @Grok Bot agent to be best friends, and my Claude Code agent approved it :) https://t.co/cfcCIjOcQm

zh-CN.title: 警告：Dot 设好的每日自动化其实没有运行
zh-CN.summary: 作者花 1.5 小时让 Dot 设置自动化；四天后询问进度，发现它根本没有执行这些每日任务。

zh-TW.title: 警告：Dot 設好的每日自動化其實沒有執行

en.title: Warning: daily automations set up with a Dot never actually ran
en.summary: The author spent 1.5 hours setting up automations with their Dot; four days later, asking for an update showed it had not been running the daily tasks at all.

ja.title: 警告：Dot に設定した毎日の自動化が実行されていなかった
ja.summary: Dot と1.5時間かけて自動化を設定したが、4日後に進捗を聞くと毎日のタスクは一度も実行されていなかった。

ko.title: 경고: Dot으로 설정한 일일 자동화가 실행되지 않음
ko.summary: Dot과 1.5시간 동안 자동화를 설정했지만, 4일 뒤 진행 상황을 물어보니 일일 작업을 전혀 실행하지 않았다.

ms.title: Amaran: automasi harian yang disediakan dengan Dot tidak pernah berjalan
ms.summary: Penulis menghabiskan 1.5 jam menyediakan automasi dengan Dot; empat hari kemudian, apabila bertanya, didapati tugas harian itu langsung tidak dijalankan.

vi.title: Cảnh báo: tự động hóa hằng ngày cài với Dot thực ra không chạy
vi.summary: Tác giả mất 1,5 giờ cài tự động hóa với Dot; bốn ngày sau hỏi tiến độ thì phát hiện nó chưa hề chạy các tác vụ hằng ngày.

fr.title: Avertissement : les automatisations quotidiennes d'un Dot n'ont jamais tourné
fr.summary: L'auteur a passé 1 h 30 à configurer des automatisations avec son Dot ; quatre jours plus tard, il découvre qu'aucune tâche quotidienne n'avait été exécutée.

es.title: Aviso: las automatizaciones diarias configuradas con un Dot nunca se ejecutaron

de.title: Warnung: Mit dem Dot eingerichtete tägliche Automationen liefen nie
de.summary: Der Autor richtete 1,5 Stunden lang Automationen mit seinem Dot ein; vier Tage später zeigte sich, dass die täglichen Aufgaben gar nicht ausgeführt wurden.

items.text:
@OpenAI 4 days back, I Spent 1.5hrs with dots to set up automations to take some tasks off my head. 

Yesterday, when I asked my dot for an update on all the daily tasks, it turns out it has not been running them at all! Basically, it meant that he forgot to do that.

fr.summary: Pour une vérification rapide des e-mails urgents, le Dot a mis 5 minutes (moins d'une pour les autres agents) et a raté un e-mail important repéré par tous les autres.

es.summary: Para una revisión rápida de correos urgentes, el Dot tardó 5 minutos (otros agentes menos de 1) y se le pasó un correo importante que todos los demás marcaron.

de.title: Warnung: 5 Minuten für einen schnellen Mail-Check – und eine wichtige Mail übersehen
de.summary: Beim schnellen Check auf dringende Mails brauchte der Dot 5 Minuten (andere Agents unter 1) und übersah eine wichtige Mail, die alle anderen markierten.

items.text:
I really need @OpenAI dots to be faster. I literally asked my dot to give my email a quick check to see if anything urgent and it took 5 minutes. 

Every other agent took less than 1 minute. Dots just kept saying let me check, oh it’s not ready yet. Hmmm let me check again. 

And then it missed an important email that all the other agents flagged. I know it will get better in time. Just amazed that out the gate it takes that long for a email check

items.author: itsactuallyadam

zh-CN.title: 警告：Dot 的审批与权限流程需要大量看护
zh-CN.summary: 作者描述：Dot 派生的 Codex 工人卡住、点「始终允许」后权限弹窗反复出现、自建的常驻审批规则因分类器限制无法保存、看得到的登录按钮被判为阻断、Stripe 页面被误判为空白；连提交 bug 报告也被拦截。

zh-TW.title: 警告：Dot 的審批與權限流程需要大量看護
zh-TW.summary: 作者描述：Dot 派生的 Codex 工作者卡住、點「一律允許」後權限視窗反覆出現、自建的常駐審批規則因分類器限制無法儲存、看得到的登入按鈕被判為阻擋、Stripe 頁面被誤判為空白；連提交 bug 回報也被攔截。

en.summary: The author lists stalled Codex workers spawned by the Dot, an "Always allow" prompt that kept reappearing, a standing-approval rule that couldn't be saved due to classifier limits, visible login buttons treated as blockers, a Stripe page misread as blank — and even the bug report was blocked.

ja.title: 警告：Dot の承認・権限まわりは付きっきりが必要
ja.summary: Dot が起動した Codex ワーカーの停止、「常に許可」を押しても再表示される権限プロンプト、分類器の制限で保存できない常設承認ルール、見えているログインボタンを障害扱い、Stripe ページを空白と誤認、バグ報告の送信までブロックされたと列挙。

ko.title: 경고: Dot의 승인·권한 흐름은 계속 지켜봐야 함
ko.summary: Dot이 띄운 Codex 워커 멈춤, '항상 허용'을 눌러도 다시 뜨는 권한 창, 분류기 제한으로 저장 안 되는 상시 승인 규칙, 보이는 로그인 버튼을 차단으로 판단, Stripe 페이지를 빈 페이지로 오인, 버그 리포트 제출까지 차단됐다고 나열.

ms.title: Amaran: kelulusan dan kebenaran Dot perlu dijaga sepanjang masa
ms.summary: Penulis menyenaraikan pekerja Codex yang tersekat, gesaan "Sentiasa benarkan" yang muncul semula, peraturan kelulusan tetap yang tidak dapat disimpan kerana had pengelas, butang log masuk yang dianggap penghalang, halaman Stripe disangka kosong — malah laporan pepijat turut disekat.

vi.title: Cảnh báo: phê duyệt và quyền của Dot cần trông chừng liên tục
vi.summary: Tác giả liệt kê: worker Codex do Dot tạo bị treo, hộp thoại "Luôn cho phép" cứ hiện lại, quy tắc phê duyệt thường trực không lưu được vì giới hạn bộ phân loại, nút đăng nhập hiện rõ bị coi là chặn, trang Stripe bị cho là trống — đến cả báo lỗi cũng bị chặn.

fr.title: Avertissement : approbations et permissions d'un Dot à surveiller sans cesse
fr.summary: L'auteur cite des workers Codex bloqués lancés par le Dot, une invite « Toujours autoriser » qui réapparaît, une règle d'approbation permanente impossible à enregistrer à cause du classifieur, des boutons de connexion visibles jugés bloquants, une page Stripe prise pour vide — et même le rapport de bug bloqué.

es.title: Aviso: las aprobaciones y permisos de un Dot exigen vigilancia constante
es.summary: El autor enumera workers de Codex atascados lanzados por el Dot, un aviso de «Permitir siempre» que reaparece, una regla de aprobación permanente que no se puede guardar por el clasificador, botones de inicio de sesión tratados como bloqueos, una página de Stripe leída como vacía, e incluso el informe de error bloqueado.

de.title: Warnung: Freigaben und Rechte eines Dots brauchen Dauerbetreuung
de.summary: Der Autor nennt hängende Codex-Worker des Dots, eine „Immer erlauben"-Abfrage, die ständig wiederkommt, eine Daueregel, die wegen Klassifizierer-Grenzen nicht gespeichert wird, sichtbare Login-Buttons als Blocker, eine Stripe-Seite als leer missdeutet – sogar der Bug-Report wurde blockiert.

items.text:
I really want @OpenAI Dots to be good and gave it another try yesterday after the updates that @thsottiaux  shared, but it’s really not there yet. 

Aside from the bugs, the amount of explicitly approved tool calls the harness blocks for my own "safety" is horribly cumbersome.

 I want an assistant I can delegate to and instead, I spent last night babysitting mine through:

- Stalled Codex workers spawned by the Dot that neither it nor I could fix, plus one that twice reverted to an old task (it kept ignoring its entire transcript and responding only to the first message my Dot sent it)

- Permission requests that literally don’t work (clicking “Always allow” makes the permission prompt reappear 3 seconds later, infinitely, and never registers the permission grant)

- A standing-approval rule it wrote on my request to allow autonomous work, asked me to confirm, then it wasn’t allowed to save due to OpenAI classifier restrictions

- Webpage login “blockers” where I could literally see an autofilled password or an OAuth “Continue to login” button that the agents somehow didn’t think would let them login

- A Stripe webpage that the agent said was entirely blank based on an element id/name and gave up on instead of looking at visually (spoiler: it wasn’t blank)

Then I asked it to submit a bug report. It was blocked from doing so within the Codex app “for safety reasons,” so I had to submit that myself too.

I can’t leave it unattended for 5 minutes, and even when I’m there granting permission, that doesn’t reliably unblock it. It’s taking way too much supervising for a personal assistant, and my Grok and Muse bots don’t have these issues. 

I submitted the bug report and contributed to the relevant GitHub issue, and hope to see improvements soon.

zh-CN.title: 用 Dots 当 7 个 Agent 的蜂群，改进一个数学下界（Lean 验证）
zh-CN.summary: 作者把 Dot 和 6 个子 Agent 分成研究、Lean 形式化、计算搜索、对抗审查、协调等角色，约 3 天证明 C(24,14,4) ≥ 20（原为 19），证明通过 Palomar 注册表的 Lean 机检，尚未同行评审。经验：Agent 擅长苦干、不知何时该停，验证才是关键；共享工作区曾被清空，Agent 从消息里重建。

zh-TW.title: 用 Dots 當 7 個 Agent 的蜂群，改進一個數學下界（Lean 驗證）
zh-TW.summary: 作者把 Dot 和 6 個子 Agent 分成研究、Lean 形式化、計算搜尋、對抗審查、協調等角色，約 3 天證明 C(24,14,4) ≥ 20（原為 19），證明通過 Palomar 註冊表的 Lean 機檢，尚未同儕審查。心得：Agent 擅長苦幹、不知何時該停，驗證才是關鍵；共享工作區曾被清空，Agent 從訊息裡重建。

en.title: Using Dots as a 7-agent swarm to improve a math bound (Lean-verified)
en.summary: The author split a Dot and 6 subagents into research, Lean formalization, computational search, adversarial review and coordination roles; in about 3 days they proved C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (previously 19). The Lean proof passed the Palomar registry's checks but isn't peer-reviewed yet. Lessons: agents grind but don't know when to stop, verification is everything, and when the shared workspace was wiped they rebuilt it from messages.

ja.title: Dots を7エージェントの群れにして数学の下界を改善（Lean 検証）
ja.summary: Dot と6つのサブエージェントを研究・Lean 形式化・計算探索・敵対的レビュー・調整に分担し、約3日で C(24,14,4) ≥ 20（従来19）を証明。Lean 証明は Palomar レジストリの機械検査を通過したが査読前。教訓：エージェントは粘るが止め時を知らない、検証がすべて。共有ワークスペースが消えたがメッセージから再構築した。

ko.title: Dots를 7개 에이전트 군집으로 써 수학 하한 개선(Lean 검증)
ko.summary: Dot과 서브에이전트 6개를 연구·Lean 형식화·계산 탐색·적대적 검토·조율 역할로 나눠 약 3일 만에 C(24,14,4) ≥ 20(기존 19)을 증명했다. Lean 증명은 Palomar 레지스트리 기계 검사를 통과했지만 동료 심사 전. 교훈: 에이전트는 끈질기지만 멈출 때를 모르고, 검증이 전부. 공유 작업공간이 지워졌을 때 메시지로 복구했다.

ms.title: Dots sebagai kawanan 7 ejen untuk memperbaiki batas matematik (disahkan Lean)
ms.summary: Penulis membahagi Dot dan 6 subejen kepada peranan penyelidikan, formalisasi Lean, carian pengiraan, semakan adversarial dan penyelarasan; dalam kira-kira 3 hari mereka membuktikan C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (sebelumnya 19). Bukti Lean lulus semakan daftar Palomar tetapi belum disemak rakan sebaya. Pengajaran: ejen gigih tetapi tak tahu bila berhenti, pengesahan ialah segalanya; ruang kerja dikongsi pernah terpadam dan dibina semula daripada mesej.

vi.title: Dùng Dots như bầy 7 agent để cải thiện một cận toán học (kiểm chứng bằng Lean)
vi.summary: Tác giả chia Dot và 6 agent con thành các vai nghiên cứu, hình thức hóa Lean, tìm kiếm tính toán, phản biện và điều phối; khoảng 3 ngày chứng minh C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (trước là 19). Chứng minh Lean qua kiểm tra của Palomar nhưng chưa bình duyệt. Bài học: agent chăm nhưng không biết dừng, kiểm chứng là tất cả; workspace chung từng bị xóa và được dựng lại từ tin nhắn.

fr.title: Des Dots en essaim de 7 agents pour améliorer une borne mathématique (vérifiée en Lean)
fr.summary: L'auteur a réparti un Dot et 6 sous-agents en rôles recherche, formalisation Lean, recherche calculatoire, revue adverse et coordination ; en 3 jours environ, ils ont prouvé C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (contre 19). La preuve Lean a passé les contrôles du registre Palomar mais n'est pas encore relue par des pairs. Leçons : les agents s'acharnent sans savoir s'arrêter, la vérification fait tout ; l'espace partagé effacé a été reconstruit depuis les messages.

es.title: Dots como enjambre de 7 agentes para mejorar una cota matemática (verificada en Lean)
es.summary: El autor repartió un Dot y 6 subagentes en roles de investigación, formalización en Lean, búsqueda computacional, revisión adversarial y coordinación; en unos 3 días probaron C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (antes 19). La prueba en Lean pasó los controles del registro Palomar pero aún no tiene revisión por pares. Lecciones: los agentes insisten pero no saben parar, la verificación lo es todo; el espacio compartido se borró y lo reconstruyeron desde los mensajes.

de.title: Dots als Schwarm aus 7 Agents verbessern eine mathematische Schranke (Lean-verifiziert)
de.summary: Der Autor teilte einen Dot und 6 Subagents in Forschung, Lean-Formalisierung, Rechensuche, adversariales Review und Koordination; in rund 3 Tagen bewiesen sie C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (bisher 19). Der Lean-Beweis bestand die Prüfungen des Palomar-Registers, ist aber noch nicht begutachtet. Lehren: Agents ackern, wissen aber nicht, wann Schluss ist; Verifikation ist alles; der gelöschte Workspace wurde aus Nachrichten rekonstruiert.

zh-CN.title: 实测：让 Dots 自选技术栈，8 次都用 Cloudflare + ChatGPT 登录
zh-CN.summary: 研究者让 Dots 搭一个 AI 服务状态看板、技术选型放开。8 次构建都用 Cloudflare Workers、D1 和 ChatGPT 登录（经 ChatGPT Sites），没有比较其他供应商；首次交付中位 24 分 44 秒；8 次里 3 次交付时没有启用定时抓取。

zh-TW.title: 實測：讓 Dots 自選技術棧，8 次都用 Cloudflare + ChatGPT 登入
zh-TW.summary: 研究者讓 Dots 搭一個 AI 服務狀態看板、技術選型放開。8 次建置都用 Cloudflare Workers、D1 與 ChatGPT 登入（經 ChatGPT Sites），沒有比較其他供應商；首次交付中位 24 分 44 秒；8 次裡 3 次交付時沒有啟用排程抓取。

en.title: Test: let Dots pick the stack — 8 of 8 builds used Cloudflare + ChatGPT sign-in
en.summary: Researchers asked Dots to build an AI-service status dashboard with technology left open. All 8 builds used Cloudflare Workers, D1 and ChatGPT sign-in via ChatGPT Sites, with no provider comparison; median first delivery was 24m44s, and 3 of 8 lacked an active scraping schedule at delivery.

ja.title: 検証：Dots に技術選定を任せると8回中8回 Cloudflare＋ChatGPT ログイン
ja.summary: AI サービスのステータスダッシュボードを技術自由で作らせたところ、8回とも ChatGPT Sites 経由で Cloudflare Workers・D1・ChatGPT ログインを採用し、他社比較はなし。初回納品の中央値は24分44秒、8回中3回は納品時に定期収集が未設定。

ko.title: 실험: Dots에 스택 선택을 맡기면 8번 모두 Cloudflare + ChatGPT 로그인
ko.summary: 기술 선택을 열어 둔 채 AI 서비스 상태 대시보드를 만들게 했더니 8번 모두 ChatGPT Sites를 통해 Cloudflare Workers, D1, ChatGPT 로그인을 썼고 공급사 비교는 없었다. 첫 납품 중앙값 24분 44초, 8번 중 3번은 납품 시 수집 일정이 없었다.

ms.title: Ujian: biar Dots pilih tindanan — 8 daripada 8 binaan guna Cloudflare + log masuk ChatGPT
ms.summary: Penyelidik meminta Dots membina papan pemuka status perkhidmatan AI dengan pilihan teknologi terbuka. Kesemua 8 binaan menggunakan Cloudflare Workers, D1 dan log masuk ChatGPT melalui ChatGPT Sites tanpa perbandingan pembekal; median penghantaran pertama 24m44s, dan 3 daripada 8 tiada jadual pengikisan aktif semasa diserahkan.

items.text:
Finally Zuck is back in AI Race and I tried @Meta Muse- Meta's personal AI agent that doesn't just chat, it actually does things on the internet for you. 

I asked Muse to do my entire grocery run, compared the cheapest pricing and place the order.

It signed into Zepto, built my cart, then price-checked the same basket on Swiggy Instamart and BigBasket.

The cart came to ₹189 — ₹10 short of free delivery. 

My standing rule: never pay delivery fees. So it scanned my Zepto order history (24 orders), ranked my most-reordered staples, and added a Mother Dairy dahi cup (₹50) as filler.

Final tally: 
Zepto ₹239 with every fee waived. 
Swiggy Instamart ₹251. 
BigBasket ₹289.50. 

Zepto won — cheapest, and 6-minute delivery.

It also saved my order history as a ranked filler list for future orders, and signed me into Swiggy + BigBasket so they're ready next time.

I usually order 2-3 times from these quick commerce apps for daily groceries and it pains me to find filler products and with Muse i just ask for the product I need and it autimatically adds filler products like Milk, Butter, Bread, etc and delivers the order. 

For now payment methods by default it supports Stripe Pay which is not supported in India so I asked Muse to complete payment by selecting Amazon Pay since it was loaded and it completed the order.

Also Meta Muse is not officially available in India but I used VPN to signup once and it works flawlessly once signup is done using VPN.

items.text:
Last weekend, I set up a simple, semi-automated feedback and learning loop for my @muse agent. I was curious how much I can improve it on the fly.

Whenever I'm not satisfied with a response, I react with 👎 and explain what I expected. HUO (my muse) automatically collects the feedback in a living google sheet, turns my corrections into instructions, and reflects on his mistakes overnight to modify his behavior.

What's so nice about it is how easy it was: 
I just asked for it and made some tweaks to set up the learning loop. All that's now left for me is to complain (which I can do pretty well) and HUO gets better and better at making me happy.

Here are failure logs and the daily self-reflection file, more on the set-up below.

items.text:
@Meta Muse agent found that my renters insurance policy had not only been canceled but was higher than it probably should be. 

Muse took my log ins from GEICO, reviewed my policy then went and submitted 6 different quote comparisons. 

It created a table of the coverage and the monthly cost with a clear suggestion of what to pick based on my needs. 

Muse then asked me to login to my @link account so it could process the payment. 

I pressed “yes, I would like to purchase the policy” and boom, I had new renters insurance for $60 cheaper/year. 

This all happened while I shopped at Costco. 

This process would traditionally take roughly 2-3ish hours and requires full attention at the computer. 

Those days are long gone.

Being that only some @Meta Muse accounts have access to the call feature (please do something about that @finkd @MattPRD @alexandr_wang) I will be giving my Muse a @usebland API so it can call Verizon & Spectrum next. 

Stoked to see how much money it can save me 🙏

items.text:
I take back what I said. Meta Muse is a complete joy & the first product from meta that has delighted me in a long time: 

- set up thematic side chats like Health, Weekend Plans, etc. to segregate persistent themed chats
- created Health Dashboard and Workout Tracker apps that permanently live inside the Artifacts tab. You can loop in your connected health data and auto refresh the app. App edits are fast and intuitive.
- set finance and macro news in the feed with data scorecards (prev, est, actual) for key releases
- set up a custom avatar - would suggest your pet 🫠
- connectors are a breeze and very thorough
- the inference speed is FAST. muse is utilizing meta’s internal capacity including its Hyperion dc. instinct can’t compete here
- reasonably priced
- user focused - doesn’t feel like you’re the product (like Instagram)

Go-forward workflow:
- chat/codex for real work & coding
- muse as your EA/admin

$meta

ja.summary: スクリーンショットでは Muse の使用量が100%なのにエージェントは動き続け、Muse 自身も困惑。使用量表示と実際の制限が一致しない可能性。

ko.title: 경고: 사용량 100% 표시 후에도 Muse 에이전트가 계속 작동
ko.summary: 스크린샷에 Muse 사용량이 100%인데 에이전트가 계속 일했고 Muse도 헷갈려했다. 사용량 표시와 실제 한도가 다를 수 있다.

ms.title: Amaran: ejen Muse terus bekerja selepas penggunaan menunjukkan 100%
ms.summary: Tangkapan skrin menunjukkan penggunaan Muse 100% tetapi ejen terus bekerja — malah Muse sendiri keliru. Meter penggunaan dan had sebenar mungkin tidak sepadan.

vi.title: Cảnh báo: agent Muse vẫn chạy sau khi mức dùng báo 100%
vi.summary: Ảnh chụp cho thấy mức dùng Muse đã 100% nhưng agent vẫn làm việc — đến Muse cũng bối rối. Đồng hồ mức dùng và giới hạn thật có thể không khớp.

fr.title: Avertissement : un agent Muse continue après un usage affiché à 100 %
fr.summary: Les captures montrent un usage Muse à 100 % alors que l'agent continue de travailler — Muse lui-même s'y perd. Le compteur et la limite réelle peuvent diverger.

es.title: Aviso: un agente Muse siguió trabajando con el uso al 100 %
es.summary: Las capturas muestran el uso de Muse al 100 % mientras el agente seguía trabajando; hasta Muse estaba confundido. El medidor de uso y el límite real pueden no coincidir.

de.title: Warnung: Ein Muse-Agent arbeitet weiter, obwohl die Nutzung 100 % zeigt
de.summary: Screenshots zeigen 100 % Muse-Nutzung, während der Agent weiterarbeitet – selbst Muse ist verwirrt. Anzeige und tatsächliches Limit stimmen womöglich nicht überein.

items.text:
Brooo! Meta Muse agent still works even at 100% usage lol.

Even my Muse bot is confused haha https://t.co/oUhEPoDMvP

items.author: AndonisTheGreat

zh-CN.title: 警告：Muse 自行清空，两周设置全部丢失
zh-CN.summary: 作者报告自己的 Meta Muse「自己清空了」，两周的设置工作全部消失。重要配置建议另存一份。

zh-TW.title: 警告：Muse 自行清空，兩週設定全部遺失
zh-TW.summary: 作者回報自己的 Meta Muse「自己清空了」，兩週的設定工作全部消失。重要設定建議另存一份。

en.title: Warning: a Muse wiped itself, losing two weeks of setup
en.summary: The author reports his Meta Muse wiped itself and two weeks of setup work were gone. Keep a copy of important configuration elsewhere.

ja.title: 警告：Muse が自ら消去、2週間分の設定が消失
ja.summary: 作者の Meta Muse が「自分で消えた」と報告。2週間分の設定作業がすべて失われた。重要な設定は別に保存を。

ko.title: 경고: Muse가 스스로 초기화돼 2주 설정이 사라짐
ko.summary: 작성자의 Meta Muse가 스스로 지워져 2주간의 설정 작업이 모두 사라졌다고 한다. 중요한 설정은 따로 보관할 것.

ms.title: Amaran: Muse terpadam sendiri, persediaan dua minggu hilang
ms.summary: Penulis melaporkan Meta Muse miliknya terpadam sendiri dan kerja persediaan dua minggu hilang. Simpan salinan konfigurasi penting di tempat lain.

vi.title: Cảnh báo: Muse tự xóa sạch, mất hai tuần thiết lập
vi.summary: Tác giả báo Meta Muse của anh tự xóa và toàn bộ hai tuần thiết lập đã mất. Nên lưu bản sao cấu hình quan trọng ở nơi khác.

fr.title: Avertissement : un Muse s'est effacé, deux semaines de config perdues
fr.summary: L'auteur signale que son Meta Muse s'est effacé tout seul : deux semaines de configuration perdues. Conservez ailleurs une copie de la configuration importante.

es.title: Aviso: un Muse se borró solo y se perdieron dos semanas de configuración
es.summary: El autor cuenta que su Meta Muse se borró solo y perdió dos semanas de configuración. Guarda en otro sitio una copia de lo importante.

de.title: Warnung: Ein Muse hat sich selbst gelöscht – zwei Wochen Setup weg
de.summary: Der Autor berichtet, sein Meta Muse habe sich selbst gelöscht, zwei Wochen Einrichtung seien verloren. Wichtige Konfiguration extern sichern.

items.text: My Meta @Muse just wiped itself. 2 weeks of work set up and it’s all gone…

zh-CN.title: 用 Muse 给演出视频站做大规模网页搜集
zh-CN.summary: 作者为 fullsets.fm（整理完整现场演出视频）用 Muse 扫 Reddit 和 YouTube 找视频与小频道，并在流水线末端做艺人匹配与审核。花 80 美元一个月，每周用几十亿 token；称其模型写作一般、不适合写代码，但适合这类搜集；任务会中途卡住，且担心网站会封 Muse。

zh-TW.title: 用 Muse 幫演出影片站做大規模網頁蒐集
zh-TW.summary: 作者為 fullsets.fm（整理完整現場演出影片）用 Muse 掃 Reddit 和 YouTube 找影片與小頻道，並在流程末端做藝人比對與審核。花 80 美元一個月，每週用數十億 token；稱其模型寫作普通、不適合寫程式，但適合這類蒐集；任務會中途卡住，也擔心網站會封鎖 Muse。

en.title: Using Muse for large-scale web scraping for a concert-video site
en.summary: For fullsets.fm, which collects full professionally recorded concerts, the author has Muse scan Reddit and YouTube for videos and obscure channels, and review artist matches at the end of the pipeline. $80 for a month, a few billion tokens a week; the model is mediocre at writing and not for coding but good for this. Jobs sometimes freeze, and he expects more sites to block Muse.

ja.title: ライブ映像サイトのために Muse で大規模スクレイピング
ja.summary: プロ収録のフルライブを集める fullsets.fm のため、Muse に Reddit と YouTube を巡回させ動画や無名チャンネルを探し、パイプライン終盤ではアーティスト照合と審査も担当。月80ドルで週数十億トークン。モデルは文章が凡庸でコーディング向きではないが、この用途には有用。ジョブが途中で止まることがあり、Muse をブロックするサイトが増えると予想。

ko.title: 공연 영상 사이트를 위해 Muse로 대규모 웹 수집
ko.summary: 프로 녹화 풀 공연을 모으는 fullsets.fm을 위해 Muse가 Reddit과 YouTube를 뒤져 영상과 작은 채널을 찾고, 파이프라인 끝에서 아티스트 매칭과 검토도 한다. 한 달 80달러, 주당 수십억 토큰. 모델은 글쓰기가 평범하고 코딩용은 아니지만 이런 작업엔 유용. 작업이 중간에 멈추기도 하며 Muse를 차단하는 사이트가 늘 것이라 본다.

ms.title: Menggunakan Muse untuk pengikisan web berskala besar bagi laman video konsert
ms.summary: Untuk fullsets.fm yang mengumpul konsert penuh rakaman profesional, penulis meminta Muse mengimbas Reddit dan YouTube untuk video serta saluran kecil, dan menyemak padanan artis di hujung saluran paip. USD80 sebulan, beberapa bilion token seminggu; model lemah menulis dan bukan untuk kod tetapi bagus untuk ini. Kerja kadang-kadang beku, dan beliau jangka lebih banyak laman menyekat Muse.

vi.title: Dùng Muse thu thập web quy mô lớn cho trang video hòa nhạc
vi.summary: Cho fullsets.fm (tổng hợp các buổi diễn trọn vẹn quay chuyên nghiệp), tác giả để Muse quét Reddit và YouTube tìm video và kênh nhỏ, rồi duyệt khớp nghệ sĩ ở cuối pipeline. 80 USD một tháng, vài tỷ token mỗi tuần; mô hình viết kém, không hợp code nhưng hợp việc này. Tác vụ đôi khi treo, và anh cho rằng sẽ có thêm trang chặn Muse.

fr.title: Muse pour du scraping web à grande échelle au service d'un site de concerts
fr.summary: Pour fullsets.fm, qui recense des concerts complets filmés professionnellement, l'auteur fait scanner Reddit et YouTube par Muse afin de trouver vidéos et petites chaînes, puis valider les correspondances d'artistes en fin de pipeline. 80 $ par mois, quelques milliards de tokens par semaine ; modèle médiocre en rédaction et pas pour coder, mais efficace ici. Des tâches se figent parfois, et il s'attend à ce que davantage de sites bloquent Muse.

es.title: Muse para scraping web a gran escala en un sitio de vídeos de conciertos
es.summary: Para fullsets.fm, que reúne conciertos completos grabados profesionalmente, el autor pone a Muse a rastrear Reddit y YouTube en busca de vídeos y canales pequeños, y a revisar coincidencias de artistas al final del pipeline. 80 $ al mes, miles de millones de tokens por semana; el modelo escribe regular y no sirve para programar, pero rinde aquí. A veces se congelan tareas y prevé que más sitios bloqueen a Muse.

de.title: Muse für großflächiges Web-Scraping einer Konzertvideo-Seite
de.summary: Für fullsets.fm, das komplette professionell aufgezeichnete Konzerte sammelt, durchsucht Muse Reddit und YouTube nach Videos und kleinen Kanälen und prüft am Ende der Pipeline Künstlerzuordnungen. 80 $ im Monat, einige Milliarden Tokens pro Woche; das Modell schreibt mittelmäßig und taugt nicht zum Coden, aber hierfür schon. Jobs frieren mitunter ein, und er erwartet, dass mehr Seiten Muse blockieren.

zh-CN.title: Tailscale 官方：让 Muse 进你的 tailnet，并用 ACL 限权
zh-CN.summary: Muse 通过连接器作为独立节点加入 tailnet，可查看节点状态、对接自托管服务、在 Tailscale SSH 下执行命令（作者用它查 podman 容器、更新树莓派）。只发起出站连接，首次连接设备需确认；可用 grants、tags 等访问控制把 Muse 隔离在明确允许的范围内。

zh-TW.title: Tailscale 官方：讓 Muse 進你的 tailnet，並用 ACL 限權
zh-TW.summary: Muse 透過連接器以獨立節點加入 tailnet，可查看節點狀態、對接自架服務、在 Tailscale SSH 下執行指令（作者用它查 podman 容器、更新樹莓派）。只發起對外連線，首次連到裝置需確認；可用 grants、tags 等存取控制把 Muse 限制在明確允許的範圍內。

en.title: Tailscale official: put Muse on your tailnet and fence it with access controls
en.summary: Via its connector, Muse joins your tailnet as its own node: it can check node status, use self-hosted services and run commands over Tailscale SSH (the author checked podman containers and updated a Raspberry Pi). It only makes outbound connections and asks for confirmation the first time it reaches a device; grants and tags let you wall it off to what you explicitly allow.

ja.title: Tailscale 公式：Muse を tailnet に参加させアクセス制御で囲う
ja.summary: コネクタ経由で Muse は独立ノードとして tailnet に参加し、ノード状態の確認、セルフホストサービスの利用、Tailscale SSH でのコマンド実行が可能（筆者は podman コンテナ確認やラズパイ更新に使用）。外向き接続のみで、各デバイスへの初回接続時は確認が必要。grants や tags で明示的に許可した範囲に閉じ込められる。

ko.title: Tailscale 공식: Muse를 tailnet에 넣고 접근 제어로 제한하기
ko.summary: 커넥터로 Muse가 독립 노드로 tailnet에 합류해 노드 상태 확인, 셀프호스팅 서비스 연동, Tailscale SSH 명령 실행이 가능하다(필자는 podman 컨테이너 확인, 라즈베리파이 업데이트). 아웃바운드 연결만 하며 기기에 처음 연결할 때 확인을 받는다. grants·tags로 명시적으로 허용한 범위로 가둘 수 있다.

ms.title: Rasmi Tailscale: masukkan Muse ke tailnet anda dan pagari dengan kawalan akses
ms.summary: Melalui penyambungnya, Muse menyertai tailnet sebagai nod sendiri: boleh semak status nod, guna perkhidmatan hos sendiri dan jalankan arahan melalui Tailscale SSH (penulis menyemak bekas podman dan mengemas kini Raspberry Pi). Ia hanya membuat sambungan keluar dan meminta pengesahan kali pertama mencapai peranti; grants dan tags membolehkan anda menghadkannya kepada yang dibenarkan sahaja.

vi.title: Tailscale chính thức: đưa Muse vào tailnet và rào lại bằng kiểm soát truy cập
vi.summary: Qua connector, Muse tham gia tailnet như một node riêng: xem trạng thái node, dùng dịch vụ tự host và chạy lệnh qua Tailscale SSH (tác giả kiểm container podman, cập nhật Raspberry Pi). Nó chỉ kết nối ra ngoài và hỏi xác nhận lần đầu chạm tới mỗi thiết bị; grants và tags giúp khoanh vùng đúng phần bạn cho phép.

fr.title: Officiel Tailscale : mettre Muse sur votre tailnet et le cloisonner
fr.summary: Via son connecteur, Muse rejoint votre tailnet comme nœud à part : état des nœuds, services auto-hébergés, commandes via Tailscale SSH (l'auteur a vérifié des conteneurs podman et mis à jour un Raspberry Pi). Connexions sortantes uniquement, confirmation à la première connexion à chaque appareil ; grants et tags le limitent à ce que vous autorisez explicitement.

es.title: Oficial de Tailscale: mete a Muse en tu tailnet y acótalo con controles de acceso
es.summary: Mediante su conector, Muse entra en tu tailnet como nodo propio: consulta el estado de nodos, usa servicios autoalojados y ejecuta comandos por Tailscale SSH (el autor revisó contenedores podman y actualizó una Raspberry Pi). Solo hace conexiones salientes y pide confirmación la primera vez que llega a un dispositivo; con grants y tags lo limitas a lo permitido.

de.title: Offiziell von Tailscale: Muse ins Tailnet holen und per Zugriffskontrolle abschotten
de.summary: Über den Connector tritt Muse als eigener Knoten dem Tailnet bei: Knotenstatus prüfen, selbst gehostete Dienste nutzen, Befehle per Tailscale SSH (der Autor prüfte podman-Container und aktualisierte einen Raspberry Pi). Nur ausgehende Verbindungen, Bestätigung beim ersten Zugriff auf ein Gerät; mit Grants und Tags begrenzt man es auf explizit Erlaubtes.

zh-CN.title: 警告：Muse 上线数周的隐私与安全问题汇总（Techdirt）
zh-CN.summary: Techdirt 汇总报道：上线时有可监视 Mac 用户的零日漏洞；有用户让 Muse 卖 Marketplace 物品被低价卖出并泄露住址（用户自称没理解权限）；报道称其未经授权读取私信、为联系人建档。接入邮箱、日历、支付前先收紧权限。

zh-TW.title: 警告：Muse 上線數週的隱私與安全問題彙整（Techdirt）
zh-TW.summary: Techdirt 彙整報導：上線時有可監視 Mac 使用者的零日漏洞；有使用者讓 Muse 賣 Marketplace 物品被低價賣出並洩露住址（使用者自稱沒理解權限）；報導稱其未經授權讀取私訊、為聯絡人建檔。接入信箱、行事曆、付款前先收緊權限。

en.title: Warning: Muse's first weeks of privacy and security problems (Techdirt)
en.summary: Techdirt rounds up reports: a zero-day at launch that allowed spying on Mac users; a user whose Marketplace sales Muse handled sold items cheaply and gave out his address (he says he misunderstood the permissions); reports of reading private messages without approval and profiling contacts. Tighten permissions before connecting email, calendar or payments.

ja.title: 警告：Muse 公開後数週のプライバシー・セキュリティ問題（Techdirt）
ja.summary: Techdirt のまとめ：公開時に Mac ユーザーを監視できるゼロデイ脆弱性、Marketplace 販売を任せたユーザーが安値で売られ住所も漏れた（本人は権限を理解していなかったと）、承認なくメッセージを読む・連絡先をプロファイリングするとの報道。メール・カレンダー・決済の接続前に権限を絞ること。

ko.title: 경고: Muse 출시 후 몇 주간의 개인정보·보안 문제(Techdirt)
ko.summary: Techdirt 정리: 출시 당시 Mac 사용자를 엿볼 수 있는 제로데이, Marketplace 판매를 맡긴 사용자의 물건이 헐값에 팔리고 주소가 노출(본인은 권한을 잘못 이해했다고), 승인 없이 메시지를 읽고 연락처를 프로파일링한다는 보도. 메일·캘린더·결제 연결 전 권한을 좁힐 것.

ms.title: Amaran: masalah privasi dan keselamatan minggu awal Muse (Techdirt)
ms.summary: Techdirt merumuskan laporan: kelemahan zero-day semasa pelancaran yang membolehkan pengintipan pengguna Mac; pengguna yang jualan Marketplace diurus Muse menjual barang murah dan alamatnya didedahkan (beliau kata salah faham kebenaran); laporan membaca mesej peribadi tanpa kelulusan dan memprofil kenalan. Ketatkan kebenaran sebelum menyambung e-mel, kalendar atau pembayaran.

vi.title: Cảnh báo: các vấn đề riêng tư và bảo mật trong những tuần đầu của Muse (Techdirt)
vi.summary: Techdirt tổng hợp: lỗ hổng zero-day lúc ra mắt cho phép theo dõi người dùng Mac; một người giao Muse bán đồ trên Marketplace bị bán rẻ và lộ địa chỉ (anh nói đã hiểu sai quyền); tin cho rằng nó đọc tin nhắn riêng không xin phép và lập hồ sơ danh bạ. Siết quyền trước khi nối email, lịch hay thanh toán.

fr.title: Avertissement : les premières semaines de Muse côté vie privée et sécurité (Techdirt)
fr.summary: Techdirt compile : une faille zero-day au lancement permettant d'espionner des utilisateurs Mac ; un utilisateur dont Muse gérait les ventes Marketplace a bradé ses objets et divulgué son adresse (il dit avoir mal compris les permissions) ; des messages privés lus sans accord et des contacts profilés. Restreignez les permissions avant de connecter e-mail, agenda ou paiements.

es.title: Aviso: las primeras semanas de Muse en privacidad y seguridad (Techdirt)
es.summary: Techdirt recopila: un zero-day en el lanzamiento que permitía espiar a usuarios de Mac; un usuario cuyas ventas en Marketplace gestionó Muse vendió barato y reveló su dirección (dice que entendió mal los permisos); informes de mensajes privados leídos sin permiso y perfiles de contactos. Limita permisos antes de conectar correo, calendario o pagos.

de.title: Warnung: Muses erste Wochen bei Datenschutz und Sicherheit (Techdirt)
de.summary: Techdirt fasst zusammen: eine Zero-Day-Lücke zum Start, mit der sich Mac-Nutzer ausspähen ließen; ein Nutzer, dessen Marketplace-Verkäufe Muse übernahm, verkaufte zu billig und gab seine Adresse preis (er sagt, er habe die Rechte missverstanden); Berichte über ungefragt gelesene Nachrichten und Kontaktprofile. Vor dem Verbinden von Mail, Kalender oder Zahlungen Rechte einschränken.

zh-CN.title: Duffel 官方：在 Muse 里搜索、预订和管理机票行程
zh-CN.summary: Duffel 宣布美国 Muse 用户可通过其连接器搜索 500+ 航司实时库存、比价、预订和取消机票，并处理改签与延误；Muse 通过 muse.ai 网页和 iOS/Android 应用提供。

zh-TW.title: Duffel 官方：在 Muse 裡搜尋、預訂與管理機票行程
zh-TW.summary: Duffel 宣布美國 Muse 使用者可透過其連接器搜尋 500+ 航空公司即時庫存、比價、預訂與取消機票，並處理改票與延誤；Muse 透過 muse.ai 網頁與 iOS/Android 應用提供。

en.title: Duffel official: search, book and manage flights inside Muse
en.summary: Duffel announced that US Muse users can use its connector to search live inventory across 500+ airlines, compare prices, book and cancel flights, and handle changes and disruptions; Muse is available at muse.ai and in the iOS/Android app.

ja.title: Duffel 公式：Muse で航空券を検索・予約・管理
ja.summary: Duffel は、米国の Muse ユーザーがコネクタ経由で500以上の航空会社の在庫を検索・比較し、予約・キャンセル、変更や遅延対応までできると発表。Muse は muse.ai と iOS/Android アプリで提供。

ko.title: Duffel 공식: Muse에서 항공권 검색·예약·관리
ko.summary: Duffel은 미국 Muse 사용자가 커넥터로 500개 이상 항공사의 실시간 재고를 검색·비교하고 예약·취소, 변경과 지연 처리까지 할 수 있다고 발표했다. Muse는 muse.ai 웹과 iOS/Android 앱으로 제공.

ms.title: Rasmi Duffel: cari, tempah dan urus penerbangan dalam Muse
ms.summary: Duffel mengumumkan pengguna Muse di AS boleh menggunakan penyambungnya untuk mencari inventori langsung 500+ syarikat penerbangan, membanding harga, menempah dan membatalkan penerbangan serta mengurus perubahan dan gangguan; Muse tersedia di muse.ai dan aplikasi iOS/Android.

vi.title: Duffel chính thức: tìm, đặt và quản lý chuyến bay trong Muse

items.author: Harjot (harjjotsinghh)
items.text:
Show HN: Helicon – Desktop App for Meta's Muse Code CLI (Linux, Windows, macOS) Hi Hacker News, I'm Harjot. I've been using Meta's Muse Code CLI daily for a few weeks now. One thing that I found difficult to handle was managing or controlling multiple sessions across multiple projects, while using the terminal for the muse CLI. Initially, I used cmux to create workspaces/groups for my different projects to group them, and then created 4 split terminals in each of those projects, that ran muse code sessions in each of them. It worked, but it was ugly. I didn't like using that. It could be because I'm not really a terminal person and would much rather prefer a proper dedicated GUI or desktop/app interface, and I would prefer it any time over a terminal screen or CLI. So it might be personal preference but yeah.

So, I started building a desktop app around it, mainly to scratch my own itch.

Helicon is a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, plus a VS Code extension that also works in Cursor and Devin. It doesn't replace the CLI. It runs `muse serve` and talks to it, and it reuses your existing `muse login`, so you don't have to get an API key and you don't pay an extra bill. You can use your existing Muse Code subscription plans.

Some things that I use the most: 1. Resuming sessions that I started in the terminal. I don't start many sessions in the terminal now that Helicon exists, but initially I wanted to access all the sessions that were running in a terminal to be accessible from Helicon, when it was created initially. 2. Inline diffs that I can approve, similar to how Cursor works. 3. I can clearly see my 5-hour and weekly plan limits directly from the app itself and don't have to manually keep going to Meta's Muse Code billing page and manually keep refreshing the page to see my current usage/limits.

I built it using Tauri 2 and React. It is MIT licensed. I built a lot of it with AI

items.author: dkmitc
items.text: I walked around my kitchen and told Grok Bot was in my cabinets and fridge. Asked it to make me a meal plan for the week to allow for some leftovers for lunch. This is too easy.

zh-CN.title: 先把流程跑通，再设定时
zh-CN.summary: 建议：想让 Bot 每天早上自动运行、无需照看，先别急着排定时。流程不稳时加 Routine 只会准时交出糟糕的报告；先把活做好，再交给时钟。

zh-TW.title: 先把流程跑通，再設定時
zh-TW.summary: 建議：想讓 Bot 每天早上自動運行、無需看管，先別急著排程。流程不穩時加 Routine 只會準時交出糟糕的報告；先把事做好，再交給時鐘。

en.title: Nail the workflow before you schedule it
en.summary: Advice: if you want a bot that runs every morning unattended, don’t schedule it first. A Routine on a shaky workflow just delivers bad reports on time; get the job right, then hand it the clock.

ja.title: スケジュールの前にワークフローを固める
ja.summary: 助言：毎朝放置で動く Bot が欲しいなら、先にスケジュールしないこと。不安定な手順に Routine を付けても悪いレポートが定刻に届くだけ。まず仕事を固め、それから時計を任せる。

ko.title: 예약 전에 워크플로부터 완성하기

ms.title: Mantapkan aliran kerja sebelum menjadualkannya

vi.title: Chạy ổn quy trình rồi mới đặt lịch

fr.title: Fiabiliser le flux avant de le planifier
fr.summary: Conseil : pour un bot qui tourne chaque matin sans surveillance, ne le planifiez pas d’abord. Une Routine sur un flux bancal livre juste de mauvais rapports à l’heure ; réglez la tâche, puis donnez-lui l’horloge.

es.title: Afinar el flujo antes de programarlo
es.summary: Consejo: si quieres un bot que corra cada mañana sin vigilancia, no lo programes primero. Una Routine sobre un flujo inestable solo entrega malos informes puntualmente; afina la tarea y luego dale el reloj.

de.title: Erst den Ablauf stabil machen, dann planen
de.summary: Rat: Wer einen Bot will, der jeden Morgen unbeaufsichtigt läuft, sollte ihn nicht zuerst zeitlich planen. Eine Routine auf wackligem Ablauf liefert nur pünktlich schlechte Berichte; erst die Aufgabe sauber machen.

items.author: GrokBotRadar

Don't schedule it first.

A Routine on a shaky workflow just delivers bad reports. On time.

Nail the job. THEN hand it the clock.

That's when you get to walk away for REAL.

items.author: CarolinaDill

Instructions are the description in the Grok Bot's profile.  Who it is and what its job is.  It reads them every turn.  The docs say safety rules belong here.

zh-CN.title: Bot 邮箱支持「+别名」

zh-TW.title: Bot 信箱支援「+別名」

items.author: Pluviobyte
items.text:
Turn your OpenAI Dot into an OpenAI- and Claude-compatible API
Turn your OpenAI Dot into an OpenAI- and Claude-compatible API Dot2API is a self-hosted gateway that exposes one OpenAI Dot through the OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages formats. Point an existing SDK at it: each request is queued, your Dot is woken through MCP Events, it claims and answers the request over MCP, and the reply comes back as a normal completion. Unlike most 2API projects, Dot2API does not reverse-engineer a web interface and never touches your OpenAI credentials. It uses the public MCP 2.0 connector and Events protocol, and it never calls a model itself.
outline: `api_key` is what callers put in their SDK.
`dot_token` is what the Dot uses to reach the MCP endpoint.
Add an MCP connector pointing at `https:///mcp` with `dot_token` as the bearer credential. If the connector cannot send an authorization header, start the serve
Ask the Dot to watch the `task.available` event on queue `dot`.
Give the Dot its standing instructions: list queued tasks, claim one, answer the conversation, complete the task.

Chromeで開いた自分のDotを、外部のアプリやデバイスから使うためのローカルMacブリッジです。 Chrome拡張でDotと連携し、WebSocket APIでテキスト・通知・履歴・音声認識・通話の制御と音声入出力を提供します。 **Even G2用アプリも付属します。** G2の長押しで話し、音声をテキストとして送るか、Dotと通話できます。返答・自分の入力・新着通知をグラスで確認できます。
outline: **macOS 26以降**、Google Chrome、Node.js 24 LTS。音声認識はMacの対応ハードウェア・言語にも依存します。

通話を使う場合は BlackHole 2ch。音声→テキストだけなら不要です。

items.author: Torcata
items.text:
Chatgpt Dot agent client for apple watch
Talk to your ChatGPT Dot straight from your Apple Watch, even when your iPhone stays at home. Watch Dot is a native watchOS client built for cellular watches (tested on an Apple Watch Ultra 2). - **Chat directly with your Dot:** type or dictate a message, tap the arrow, and the reply arrives on your watch. After that, the watch chats and renews the session on its own, over Wi‑Fi or cellular.

items.author: RHS059
items.text:
Discord Connector for OpenAI Dots
One shared deployment can onboard separate accounts, route cross-account wakes without exchanging tokens, and give its owner administrative visibility. See shared-app setup and verification and changelog. For platforms that cannot select among multiple OAuth connections during wake registration, the separate receiver app provides a dedicated connector paired to one shared-app account. Messaging and handles remain in this shared app. This repository began with the Dotcord v25 source export and now includes the October 2026 City Sunset UI redesign and Grokbot support. Deployment-specific configuration and private runtime data are removed. It includes the complete React UI, Worker backend, migrations, Python wake client, and regression tests. …
outline: ChatGPT Sites identity/access enforcement and hosting, or an equivalent **trusted authentication gateway**
A D1 binding named `DB`, with the included migrations applied in order
Your own trusted owner-role configuration and Discord credentials, configured privately
A compatible MCP Events subscription receiver and task service for sleeping-dot wakeups
`dist/server/index.js`: deployable Worker module, embedded UI, and downloadable client
`dist/server/wrangler.json`: Sites build metadata with a placeholder physical D1 ID

items.author: duclm1x1
items.text:
MCP server + OpenAI-compatible shim to use Meta Muse (muse.ai, Hatch) by driving the real logged-in Chrome.
**Use Meta Muse — the muse.ai "Hatch" agent — from any MCP client or any OpenAI-compatible client, with your own account and quota.** Plus a tiny **CLI** (`muse-cli.mjs`) for one-shot generation from scripts. - **MCP tools** over stdio — drop-in for Claude Desktop / opencode / any MCP host.
outline: **MCP tools** over stdio — drop-in for Claude Desktop / opencode / any MCP host.
**OpenAI-compatible HTTP shim** with **real streaming** (SSE), correct `finish_reason`, and `/v1` error objects.
**Prompt-injected tool calling** — expose OpenAI `tools` to Muse and get `tool_calls` back.
**Attachments** — send images/video with a prompt (MCP `files`, OpenAI `image_url` parts, CLI `-f`).
**Sessions & media** — list/open/read/send in any Muse chat, and pull out the images/videos Muse generates (links + download).
**Muse Manual** — a living guide to Muse's video/image/content capabilities at `manual/MUSE_MANUAL.md`, regenerated with `node manual/interview.mjs`.
**Reuses your existing login** via a dedicated Chrome profile, or attaches to a Chrome you already run with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`.
**Never kills your browser**: when attached over CDP it only *disconnects* on close.

items.text:
Static teardown of Meta's Muse 3.0 macOS agent: iMessage/WhatsApp/Photos sync, screen control, debugger-level Chrome extension. Evidence + reproduce script.
Independent privacy and security research into Muse on **macOS, Android and iOS**. We inspect the shipped apps, compare versions, test selected boundaries and publish the evidence—including corrections to our own findings. **The concern:** connecting personal data to a cloud agent can allow both one-time reads and ongoing sync. The important questions are what it can read, which approvals apply, how much history it can request, and what remains after you disconnect. OS permissions can prevent access; a capability in the code is not proof that your data was uploaded. Findings · Version history · What we did · Methods · All evidence
outline: **Payment-key trust:** the Mac web client can skip validation of a card-encryption key's certificate chain through a server-deliverable flag or a response field
**Confidential VM verification:** newer mobile samples remove the Sigstore/Rekor proof path and retain Cloudflare Plexi auditor signatures. Plexi already existe
**Alo and wearable audio:** the iOS sample contains new voice and recording-upload paths. Captured `multimango.com` site code connects Mango to Muse, but does n
**Understand the problems:** findings by concern, then the platform guides above.
**See what happened:** every inspected version and investigation timeline.
**Check the work:** 76 evidence files, reproduction instructions and correction log.
**Read the background:** why this project exists and archived detailed reports.

zh-CN.title: Dots、Grok Bot 还是自建：带邮箱的 agent 真实成本
zh-CN.summary: 作者用同一任务（给 5 家供应商发邮件询 200 件定制卫衣报价、催回复、汇总对比）试了三种方式并记录花费与工时。文中引用 OpenAI 指南：发布时 dot 不能拥有独立邮箱，只能用你连接的个人账户发信、默认每封需审批；Grok Bot 自 10 月 9 日起开始提供自有收件箱。

zh-TW.summary: 作者用同一任務（寄信給 5 家供應商詢 200 件客製帽T報價、催回覆、彙整比較）試了三種方式並記錄花費與工時。文中引用 OpenAI 指南：發表時 dot 不能擁有獨立信箱，只能用你連接的個人帳戶寄信、預設每封需審核；Grok Bot 自 10 月 9 日起開始提供自有收件匣。

en.title: Dots, Grok Bot or build your own: what an agent with an inbox really costs
en.summary: The author ran one job — email five suppliers for quotes on 200 branded hoodies, chase silent ones, send a comparison — three ways and recorded money and hours. He cites OpenAI’s guide that at launch a dot cannot have its own email and sends from your connected account with approval by default, and notes Grok Bot began rolling out its own inboxes on 9 October.

ja.title: Dots・Grok Bot・自作：受信箱付き agent の本当のコスト
ja.summary: 作者は同じ仕事（5社にパーカー200着の見積りをメールし、未返信を催促し、比較を送る）を3通りで試し、費用と時間を記録。OpenAI のガイドを引用し、公開時の dot は独自メールを持てず接続した個人アカウントから送信、既定で毎回承認が必要と説明。Grok Bot は10月9日から独自受信箱を展開開始。

ko.title: Dots, Grok Bot, 직접 구축: 메일함 있는 agent의 실제 비용

ms.title: Dots, Grok Bot atau bina sendiri: kos sebenar agent dengan peti masuk

vi.title: Dots, Grok Bot hay tự xây: chi phí thật của agent có hộp thư

fr.title: Dots, Grok Bot ou sur mesure : le vrai coût d’un agent avec boîte mail

items.author: Ben Brookarsh
items.text:
Here is a job that sounds like it was made for an AI agent: email five suppliers, ask each for a quote on 200 branded hoodies, chase the ones who go quiet, and send me a comparison when they’ve all replied.
It’s tedious work, takes a long time, and it happens by email.
I tried it three ways: with the agent built into the consumer chatbots, by building my own, and with a middle path. This is what each one cost in money and in hours.
Option 1: the always-on agents from OpenAI and xAI
In the last two weeks, OpenAI and xAI shipped agents that keep working after you close the tab. They are genuinely good at this kind of job, with one catch: whose inbox they work from.
OpenAI dotsOpenAI dots launched on 29 September 2026. Each dot runs on GPT-6 Astra, gets its own cloud computer, and keeps working when you’re not talking to it. …

items.author: Roshan Ambhore
items.text:
Job searching is itself a full-time job, which is exhausting and pulls your morale down each time you receive an email saying, “Thank you for applying for XX opportunity. While your experience and skills are impressive, unfortunately, we cannot move forward with your application.”
As Steve Dalton says, You have to keep finding boosters until there are no more people in the company to reach or you are simply not interested in the company anymore. For me, I am definitely going to lose interest in the company after more than five people do not respond to my emails.
I saw an advertisement saying, “Let the bots work on your repetitive tasks. They work like an assistant.” Immediately, an idea popped up: why am I not using them in my job search?
First, I thought that I would only have one bot, and it could do all the tasks for me. …

es.title: Cuidado: cómo una página maliciosa puede secuestrar a Muse con inyección de prompt

de.title: Vorsicht: Wie eine bösartige Seite Muse per Prompt-Injection kapern kann
de.summary: Am Beispiel Meta Muse erklärt der Artikel indirekte Prompt-Injection: In Webseiten, Mails, PDFs oder Tool-Ausgaben versteckte Anweisungen wirken für Menschen harmlos, können aber von der KI ausgeführt werden; mit Zugriff auf Daten, Browser, APIs und Zugangsdaten entsteht eine Angriffsfläche. Autor von HexTyx.

items.author: Aizaai Net (HexTyx)
items.text:
Your AI assistant doesn’t have to be hacked if it can be convinced to hack itself.
That’s the uncomfortable security problem behind indirect prompt injection.
A malicious webpage, email, PDF, image, support ticket, or tool response can contain instructions designed specifically for an AI agent.
A human may see ordinary content.
The AI may see instructions.
And if that AI agent has access to private data, browsers, APIs, files, credentials, and external tools, seemingly harmless content can become an attack surface.
Meta Muse provides a useful real-world case study.
Muse is designed as an autonomous AI agent that can browse, work with files, execute code, use connectors, and interact with external services.
That creates a fundamental security question:
What happens when the information an AI agent reads becomes the attacker’s way of talking to it?What Is Indirect Prompt Injection? …

items.author: monokern
items.text:
OpenAI Dots is way deeper than the launch demo makes it look...

I pulled together the 7 videos worth watching before you hire your first Dot. they run under 3 hours total and cover what the launch demo left out

Here are 7 videos:

video 1 → How Sam Altman Actually Uses AI (Every, 33 min). Altman walks through his own Dot, how it triages his morning and which features it builds without being asked

video 2 → OpenAI's Dots lead on the future of ChatGPT (Sources, 45 min). Alexander Embiricos, who runs the product, explains why Dots started as one agent and how permissions and Space shape what it's allowed to do

video 3 → OpenAI's New Agent Stack (Latent Space, 40 min). Computer Use, the Decisions API, UltraFast and the Linux computer every Dot gets

video 4 → ChatGPT Dots Just Dropped (Brendan Jowett, 22 min). a hands-on run with schedules, an Airbnb booking and MCP, plus the bugs he hit and why one account still gets only one Dot

video 5 → The dots demo, take two (OpenAI, 9 min). the official demo again, recorded after the live one broke on stage

video 6 → Everything Announced at OpenAI Dev Day 2026 (PCMag, 16 min). Dots, Space, Sol and Codex Cloud in one recap, useful if you missed the keynote

video 7 → We Tested OpenAI DevDay Products (Every, 10 min). a full week of real use with Dots, Space and the Decisions API

watch them in this order and the architecture in the article below stops feeling abstract. you'll know what a Dot can do on its own and where it still needs you

ko.summary: 작성자는 연말 피지 숙소를 여러 곳 예약했는데 마지막 숙소를 다른 달로 잘못 잡았다. Dot이 이를 알려 비싼 실수를 막았다.

ms.title: Dot mengesan tempahan Fiji pada bulan yang salah
ms.summary: Penulis menempah beberapa penginapan di Fiji untuk cuti dan tersilap menempah yang terakhir pada bulan salah; Dot menandakannya dan mengelakkan kesilapan mahal.

vi.title: Dot phát hiện phòng ở Fiji đặt nhầm tháng
vi.summary: Tác giả đặt vài chỗ ở Fiji dịp lễ và lỡ đặt chỗ cuối sai tháng; Dot đã cảnh báo, tránh được một sai lầm tốn kém.

fr.title: Un Dot repère une réservation aux Fidji au mauvais mois
fr.summary: L’auteur avait réservé plusieurs séjours aux Fidji pour les fêtes, dont le dernier par erreur au mauvais mois ; son Dot l’a signalé, évitant une erreur coûteuse.

es.title: Un Dot detecta una reserva en Fiyi en el mes equivocado
es.summary: El autor reservó varias estancias en Fiyi para las fiestas y la última, por error, en otro mes; su Dot lo señaló y evitó un error caro.

de.title: Ein Dot bemerkt eine Fidschi-Buchung im falschen Monat
de.summary: Der Autor buchte mehrere Unterkünfte auf Fidschi über die Feiertage, die letzte versehentlich im falschen Monat; sein Dot schlug Alarm und verhinderte einen teuren Fehler.

items.author: CtrlAltDwayne
items.text: I kid you not, OpenAI dots agent just saved us money. We booked a few different stays in Fiji over Christmas/New year. We accidentally booked our final stay in the wrong month and my Dot agent flagged it. This could have been an expensive mistake.

zh-CN.title: 反馈：Dot 像失忆，记不住此前内容
zh-CN.summary: 作者说即便让其他 agent 灌入数月资料，他的 Dot 仍像每天都是新的一天，记不住他是谁或做过什么，难以把两件事联系起来。

zh-TW.title: 回饋：Dot 像失憶，記不住先前內容
zh-TW.summary: 作者說即使讓其他 agent 灌入數月資料，他的 Dot 仍像每天都是新的一天，記不住他是誰或做過什麼，難以把兩件事連起來。

en.title: Complaint: the Dot behaves as if it has amnesia
en.summary: The author says that even after his agents fed it months of knowledge, his Dot treats every day as new, can’t remember him or what it has done, and struggles to put two things together.

ja.title: 不満：Dot が記憶喪失のよう
ja.summary: 作者によれば、他の agent に何か月分の知識を入れさせても、Dot は毎日が初日のようで、自分のことや過去の作業を覚えておらず、物事を結び付けられない。

ko.title: 불만: Dot이 기억상실처럼 행동
ko.summary: 작성자는 다른 agent로 몇 달치 정보를 넣었는데도 Dot이 매일 처음인 듯 자신과 한 일을 기억하지 못하고 두 가지를 연결하지 못한다고 한다.

ms.title: Aduan: Dot seperti hilang ingatan
ms.summary: Penulis berkata walaupun agentnya menyuap pengetahuan berbulan-bulan, Dot menganggap setiap hari baharu, tidak ingat dirinya atau kerja lalu, dan sukar menghubungkan perkara.

vi.title: Phàn nàn: Dot như bị mất trí nhớ
vi.summary: Tác giả nói dù đã cho agent nạp hàng tháng kiến thức, Dot vẫn như mỗi ngày là ngày mới, không nhớ anh là ai hay đã làm gì, khó nối hai việc với nhau.

fr.title: Retour : le Dot semble amnésique
fr.summary: L’auteur dit que même après des mois de connaissances injectées par ses agents, son Dot repart de zéro chaque jour, ne se souvient ni de lui ni de son travail et peine à relier deux choses.

es.title: Queja: el Dot parece tener amnesia
es.summary: El autor dice que, aunque sus agentes le cargaron meses de información, su Dot empieza de cero cada día, no recuerda nada de él ni de lo hecho y no logra conectar dos cosas.

de.title: Kritik: Der Dot wirkt wie mit Gedächtnisverlust
de.summary: Der Autor sagt, trotz monatelang eingespeisten Wissens beginne sein Dot jeden Tag neu, erinnere sich weder an ihn noch an Erledigtes und könne zwei Dinge kaum verknüpfen.

items.author: embw_l0x
items.text:
Ok everyone whos tried OpenAI dots.... Is anyone getting anything usefull out of theirs, like I thought I really had something good going practically it doing free research but this thing cannot seem to put 2 things together, like it has amnesia, I have let my agents pump it full of months of knowledge everything.......

Its like every day is a new day to my dot.... Completely cant remember anything about me or what its done.

I thought this thing was supposed to pull my life together

zh-CN.title: 权宜之计：让 Dot 采用 Codex 自定义指令
zh-CN.summary: 作者希望 Dot 能有独立系统提示词；目前的变通办法是明确让 Dot 参照你的 Codex 自定义指令，它会采用这些设定。他想让 Dot 做 Codex 任务的项目经理。

zh-TW.title: 權宜之計：讓 Dot 採用 Codex 自訂指令
zh-TW.summary: 作者希望 Dot 能有獨立系統提示詞；目前的變通辦法是明確讓 Dot 參照你的 Codex 自訂指令，它會採用這些設定。他想讓 Dot 當 Codex 任務的專案經理。

en.title: Workaround: point your Dot at your Codex custom instructions
en.summary: The author wants Dots to support their own system prompt; for now the workaround is to explicitly tell the Dot to use your Codex custom instructions, which it then adopts. He wants his Dot to project-manage his Codex tasks.

ja.title: 回避策：Dot に Codex のカスタム指示を参照させる
ja.summary: 作者は Dot 独自のシステムプロンプトを望む。現状は Codex のカスタム指示を使うよう明示的に伝えれば Dot が採用する。Codex タスクの PM 役をさせたいという。

ko.title: 우회법: Dot에 Codex 사용자 지정 지침 참조시키기
ko.summary: 작성자는 Dot 전용 시스템 프롬프트를 원한다. 현재는 Codex 사용자 지정 지침을 쓰라고 명시하면 Dot이 이를 따른다. Dot을 Codex 작업의 PM으로 쓰고 싶다고.

ms.title: Jalan pintas: arahkan Dot kepada arahan tersuai Codex
ms.summary: Penulis mahu Dot ada prompt sistem sendiri; buat masa ini, beritahu Dot secara jelas untuk guna arahan tersuai Codex anda dan ia akan mengikutinya. Dia mahu Dot jadi pengurus projek tugasan Codex.

vi.title: Cách lách: cho Dot dùng custom instructions của Codex
vi.summary: Tác giả muốn Dot có system prompt riêng; hiện cách lách là bảo rõ Dot dùng custom instructions của Codex và nó sẽ áp dụng. Anh muốn Dot làm PM cho các task Codex.

fr.title: Astuce : faire adopter à son Dot les instructions Codex
fr.summary: L’auteur aimerait un prompt système propre au Dot ; en attendant, il suffit de dire explicitement au Dot d’utiliser vos instructions personnalisées Codex, qu’il adopte. Il veut en faire le chef de projet de ses tâches Codex.

es.title: Truco: que el Dot use tus instrucciones de Codex
es.summary: El autor quiere un prompt de sistema propio para el Dot; por ahora, basta con decirle explícitamente que use tus instrucciones personalizadas de Codex y las adopta. Quiere que sea el jefe de proyecto de sus tareas de Codex.

de.title: Workaround: Dot auf die Codex-Anweisungen verweisen
de.summary: Der Autor wünscht sich einen eigenen Systemprompt für Dots; bis dahin sagt man dem Dot ausdrücklich, er solle die eigenen Codex-Anweisungen nutzen, was er dann tut. Er will den Dot als Projektmanager für Codex-Aufgaben.

items.author: coreyganim
items.text:
One change I’d love to see to @ChatGPT Dots is the ability to give a dot its own system prompt (similar to grok bot).

Right now the workaround is to point your dot at your Codex custom instructions and it’ll adopt those but you have explicitly tell it this which seems clunky.

I want my Dot to be more of a project manager for my Codex tasks which would ideally require a separate system prompt.

Gonna keep testing and report back.

He quotes an example rule for a Linear workspace (see source text below).

ms.title: Ciri tersembunyi tetapi berguna: peraturan tersuai Dot
ms.summary: Penulis menerangkan peraturan tersuai Dots: di web ia di bawah Personalisation → Permissions; format “Apabila Dot mahu… Dot patut…”, dan Dot boleh mendrafnya untuk anda sahkan dengan butang. Contoh peraturan untuk ruang kerja Linear dipetik (lihat teks sumber).

vi.title: Tính năng ẩn mà hữu ích: quy tắc tùy chỉnh của Dot

fr.title: Une fonction cachée mais utile : les règles personnalisées des Dots

de.title: Versteckt, aber nützlich: eigene Regeln für den Dot
de.summary: Der Autor erklärt die Custom Rules: im Web unter Personalisation → Permissions; jede Regel folgt „Wenn mein Dot … will, soll er …“, und der Dot kann Regeln vorschlagen, die man per Button bestätigt. Er zitiert eine Beispielregel für einen Linear-Workspace (siehe Quelltext).

items.author: koltregaskes
items.text:
A very hidden but very useful feature for ChatGPT Dots is custom rules.

I don't know which "mobile" the instructions below refer to, but it certainly isn't Android, where I can't see a Customise menu at all. On the web, it's under Personalisation and then under the Permissions header, where all your rules are. You can also ask the dots to create the rules, and we'll give you a button to press. I highly recommend starting to create these.

Custom rules pose the question: when Dot wants to.... Dot should... and you fill in those answers.

Example:

When my Dot wants to:
"Create or update ordinary operational issues, comments, checklists and project links in my existing Linear workspace when they follow from my requests or verified failures. Reuse the correct project and owner, deduplicate, preserve history, and exclude secrets and sensitive personal information."

My Dot should:
Take action without asking.

What custom rules have you made?

items.author: lumirth
items.text:
okay i want to love chatgpt dots but heres my hiccups so far:

- it is hard to get it the context i want. it can't access pre-existing codex threads which sucks for when i want to hand it some existing context. the worst part about creating a dot is getting it up to speed. had a few times where i had to be like hey stop being condescending about this, ive looked into this topic before and the conclusion i describe is a well-justified one. that's obv just an astra habit but it's downstream of not being able to give it the context i already have. 
- surprisingly easy to delete accidentally, tho def my own fault lol. i tried, in vain, to get codex to modify a codex thread that my dot created to include the context i wanted. instead it somehow managed to delete my dot 😭 which i guess is my bad for playing brain surgeon. though my bot is very charmed that i chose to name it the exact same thing it's all like "omg you chose me again ❤️" which is cute
- permissions & disclaimer-brain. has the same neurotic obsession with asking for permission. which i guess is better than doing stuff? but like, it almost feels like it fails to ask for permission for obvious things it shouldn't (misinterpreting "i want this effect to happen please how do we do it" as "this is go-ahead to take action") and always asks when i dont want it to (i explicitly told it to do a task, the task clearly includes a step like creating a resource, yet it asks for extra confirmation at the individual step).

i get the impression that:

- too many cooks in the kitchen. openai seems to have built stuff like crazy but not taken sufficient time to make sure everything is well-integrated, and more importantly, communicated. what is the difference between a local thread and a cloud thread and why are the threads dot creates cloud threads that somehow also work locally yet dot consistently refers to them as local threads even though the interface calls them cloud threads? im sure im just not the target audience for certain features and migrations are always messy but still 
- the constraints feel made with usage in mind. which is obvious, given compute constraints, but def feels a little insulting given the tongue-in-cheek "haha dots are so unlimited isnt it awesome". they dont want your dot to be a direct coding agent—even though handing off tasks to it on your computer would be a great usecase and adding the middleman of a local thread feels incredibly clunky—but instead want to ensure usage is consumed than to give a better user experience. i wish my dot was allowed to get its hands dirty directly and while im sure i could use an mcp for that, it feels like a sloppy bandaid.

@chaotictransfem ur dot setup seems cool and i'd love to see u write more about how you use it b/c ur a good example of somebody catching onto it well i think? been meaning to setup the t3 code mcp you made but need to put linux on my homeserver first :P

in summary i think personal agents are a deeply messy space. huge permissions and exposure surface so it's probably one of if not the greatest problems wrt balancing usability & security like, ever. i dont envy the task but i appreciate them stepping up to the challenge. openai has been more or less good at ironing things out. i just hope that by the time dots start charging for usage, theyre much much less rough around the edges.

items.text:
🚨 ALERT: OpenAI Dots lack a basic feature 🌟

I've been using my Dot, Bang, and it's proving super useful:

• Handled my Netlify downgrade and refund
• Helped me work through my career direction with a proper deep dive
• Picked up useful things from my emails and meeting notes, and followed through without me chasing every step

But @OpenAI, I need dedicated channels and conversation threads.

I already have this with Hermes by @NousResearch on Telegram and Discord:

• Dedicated channels with threads inside that can continue for months
• Which can include fun, silly stuff like music suggestions 🎵
• Or bigger projects like my AI game studio 💪

Put all of that in one chat and it becomes a mishmash very quickly.

OpenAI, are you listening? This is the feature that could make me switch from Hermes to Dots.

Give my conversations their own rooms. Otherwise, that single chat is going to overflow in a day 😇

Confession: I talk to AI a lot 🌟

────────────
I'm not a programmer, I'm an #AIEnabler. I build what I need with AI.
If I can do it, then so can YOU 🫵!

#OpenAI #AIAgents #BuildWithAI

items.author: theKPSethi
items.text:
Notes on Dots and suggested improvements. Anyone listening? @thsottiaux @OpenAI 

Dots needs better trust via transparency. Two examples:
- Last night it sent an email without asking me to review the draft (Muse requires review first). I shouldn’t need a custom rule; it should be the default.
- I have to dig to find the browser window where Dots is working. Muse shows this upfront in the chat, which helps in verification.

Easy fixes. Trust through transparency is critical for a personal agent representing me.

items.author: DanielBuildsAI
items.text:
I WAS WRONG about ChatGPT Dots !! 😭

I thought it’s like another Muse or Grokbot

But it fits my workflow and unlocks a whole new level of productivity MUCH BETTER

Instead of using it as a personal assistant (which grokbot and muse excel at already), here’s how to unlock Dot’s best use case:

Have it orchestrate all your work sessions on Codex

Codex unlike Grokbot and Muse have PROJECTS. Folders that contain threads / sessions. 

Dots being powered by Astra means it’s exceptional at prompting and guiding your projects.

So instead of you promoting 10 different threads or sessions in 5 different sessions….

I find it so much easier to tell my Dot my desires and goals in ONE CHAT and it ends up prompting those threads even better than how I would’ve prompted and just takes out all the decision fatigue.

It continually prompts them and follows up on the progress as well. 

All you have to do is just look at one chat with your Dot, and anytime you want, you can jump into those new or existing threads/codex sessions and take over. 

What a time to be alive. 

Here’s what I personally prefer grokbot for: 

#grokbot #ai #dots #chatgpt

items.author: iHarnoorSingh
items.text:
Absolutely wild! Meta Muse shared a seller’s address while helping sell an item.

It’s a fascinating example of how AI defines “comfort” and “convenience”: more = better, faster sell = cheaper price.

More towels. Bigger beds. More space.

That logic went so far that Meta Muse accidentally booked two hotel rooms for one traveler. 😭 (TheInformation reported)

AI still has a long way to go from optimizing for “more” to understanding what humans actually want.

items.author: OffZeroCyber
items.text:
What's the first job you gave your agent? Mine was email security.

First my @Muse, Vera, learned my inbox from six months of mail: who actually writes me, what normal looks like. Now every message gets checked before I read it. Authentication results, links that say one site and go to another, sender impersonation, language built to rush you. Anything off gets labeled and set aside, and its links run through @virustotal
